rv.q: Even at its most extreme, The Steel Man is all too real, and its current staging makes for an unforgettable night at the theatre.
The trouble is that the story promises more fireworks than it ultimately delivers.
The story is realistic and sympathetic, yet dramatization just misses.
What it lacks is the emotional complexity that would allow its central relationship to transcend cruelty and obligation.

cn.t: Gitter's family drama earns praise for its visceral emotional power and forceful examination of Holocaust trauma's intergenerational impact. Critics commend the play's compelling exploration of a survivor's unresolved anguish shaping his relationship with his son.
